facts.statement: Fossils of Tianyuornis were found in lake deposits within the Yixian Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Tianyuornis was unearthed from lake deposits in the Yixian Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.

facts.statement: Tianyuornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically from the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Tianyuornis is a genus of ornithuromorph birds from the Early Cretaceous period (Barremian to Aptian stages).

facts.statement: Tianyuornis was roughly the same size as modern phoebes.
facts.quote: Tianyuornis, like its other relatives, was similar in size to modern phoebes.

facts.statement: Tianyuornis is distinguished by unique features including a straight lower jaw and teeth preserved in both the upper and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Tianyuornis however, also possesses several autapomorphies such as a straight dentary, and teeth that were preserved in the maxilla and mandible.

facts.statement: Tianyuornis is classified as a genus of ornithuromorph birds.
facts.quote: Tianyuornis is a genus of ornithuromorph birds

facts.statement: Tianyuornis belongs to the family Hongshanornithidae.
The type species of the genus Tianyuornis is Tianyuornis cheni.
Tianyuornis lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The presence of teeth in Tianyuornis supports the controversial hypothesis that other members of the Hongshanornithidae family also possessed teeth.
facts.quote: The possession of teeth reveals new and important morphological information of hongshanornithids, as well as confirms the controversial presence of teeth of the members of Hongshanornithidae.

rejected.statement: A nearly complete subadult fossil of Tianyuornis revealed a small body and elongated hindlimbs.
rejected.quote: A nearly complete and articulated subadult individual has been recovered from the Yixian Formation, this individual had a small body and elongate hindlimbs.
